decisions.reasoning: This is decision number 1 with no prior attempts, no fixes applied, and no latest verification — so the correct first move is to run the standard render and see what the gates say. Looking at the current findings: picture_area passes (480×412, no padding), pose_coverage passes at 1.0 (gate requires ≥0.6), one_subject passes at 1.0 (gate requires ≥0.95), subject_size passes with p50 0.338 / p95 0.345 well under the 0.55 cap, and distance_steady passes at 1.16× (gate requires ≤1.35). The only non-passing items are warnings (headroom: crown outside on 78% of frames — recorded-content limit, not a defect to fix; face_exposure: gain held at ×0.80 — also a warning within the fgexp_clamp bounds) and an info item (key_direction). No gate has been measured as failing yet because no composite has been attempted. The matte_extent, separation, head_spread, head_drift, frame_count, and audio_md5 gates all require a rendered output to evaluate. process.standard is the designated standard strategy for a first attempt and has no gate-failure prerequisite. If this attempt reveals failing gates that process.standard doesn't address (e.g. separation), the next decision can select process.separation_targeted, which addresses separation and has 2 retries remaining in the budget.

The latest verification (attempt_1) failed on exactly one gate: separation (id "separation"), which measured 1.00× against the required ≥1.5× — short by 0.50×. All other gates passed: pose_coverage 1.0, one_subject 1.0, matte_extent 1.018, head_spread 0.006, head_drift 1.5 px, frame_count 2116, and audio_md5 equal. The standard process (process.standard) used rimamt 0.28 and lwamt 0.5, which was insufficient to lift the edge luma ratio. The allowed strategy process.separation_targeted directly addresses the "separation" gate and permits stronger rim and light wrap (rimamt_max 0.45, lwamt_max 0.7) plus a bounded shadow lift (shadow_lift_max 0.04) and fgexp clamped to [0.8, 1.25], all without altering the performer's pixels. The retry budget shows 0 reprocesses used against a budget of 2, so there is one remaining slot after this attempt. If this also fails the separation gate and the budget is exhausted, the honest exit is reshoot with guidance to avoid wearing deep-red/burgundy tones that blend into the stage curtain.

Both allowed process strategies have now been exhausted. Attempt 1 used process.standard and failed separation with a value of 1.45× against the required 1.5×. Attempt 2 pushed process.separation_targeted to its absolute bounds (rimamt 0.45, lwamt 0.7, shadow_lift 0.04, fgexp 0.8 — all at their maximums per the strategy's bounds) and still only reached 1.45×, still 0.05× short of the 1.5× gate. The retry budget of 2 reprocesses is now fully spent (reprocesses_used: 1, meaning one non-standard retry consumed, and both strategies have been run). No fix strategy addresses the separation gate — fix.reframe only addresses picture_area and subject_size. The root cause, per the separation finding, is that the edge luma inside (0.173) vs outside (0.119) is too close: the performer's outfit or the recording conditions don't give enough contrast against the deep red curtain. The reshoot guidance is clear: don't wear colors that blend with the stage — the curtain is deep red, so no red, maroon, burgundy or hot pink; mid-tone neutrals, blue, green or a pattern should separate by about 3×. The face is also over-lit (face luma 0.727, held at ×0.80 gain), and the crown is outside the picture on 78% of frames. The performer should also stand further back or reframe so the crown is within the picture, and use a softer front light to bring face luma closer to 0.46.
